metrics_comparison.quantitative_results: On question answering HotpotQA and fact verification Fever, ReAct overcomes prevalent hallucination and error propagation in chain-of-thought reasoning by interacting with a simple Wikipedia API and generates human-like task-solving trajectories that are more interpretable than baselines without reasoning traces. On interactive decision making benchmarks ALFWorld and WebShop, ReAct outperforms imitation and reinforcement learning methods by an absolute success rate of 34% and 10% respectively, with improved human interpretability and trustworthiness over state-of-the-art baselines.
metrics_comparison.baseline_comparison: Consistently outperforms Act-only and standard Chain-of-Thought (CoT) baselines across QA, fact verification, and interactive decision tasks.

evaluated_datasets: Zero-shot evaluation on general language modeling and reasoning benchmarks and tool-specific probes for arithmetic, factual question answering, search, translation and calendar use. Evaluation covers common downstream tasks such as LAMBADA, HellaSwag, PIQA and similar zero-shot benchmarks, plus custom tool-use assessments measuring accuracy of calculator, QA, search and translation calls.
metrics_comparison.quantitative_results: Toolformer achieves substantially improved zero-shot performance across a variety of downstream tasks, often competitive with much larger models, without sacrificing core language modeling abilities. Tool use improves arithmetic accuracy, factual correctness and translation quality, and the model autonomously decides which APIs to call to obtain useful information for text completion.
metrics_comparison.baseline_comparison: Consistently outperforms Act-only and standard Chain-of-Thought (CoT) baselines across QA, fact verification, and interactive decision tasks.

metrics_comparison.quantitative_results: Reflexion obtains significant improvements over a baseline agent across diverse tasks including sequential decision-making, coding, and language reasoning. On HumanEval coding benchmark, Reflexion achieves 91% pass@1 accuracy, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art GPT-4 that achieves 80%.
metrics_comparison.baseline_comparison: Consistently outperforms Act-only and standard Chain-of-Thought (CoT) baselines across QA, fact verification, and interactive decision tasks.

metrics_comparison.quantitative_results: ToT significantly enhances problem-solving abilities over Chain of Thought on three novel planning/search tasks. On Game of 24, GPT-4 with chain-of-thought prompting solves ~4% of tasks while ToT achieves ~74% success rate. Improvements are also shown on Creative Writing and Mini Crosswords, demonstrating gains from deliberate multi-path exploration and self-evaluation.
metrics_comparison.baseline_comparison: Consistently outperforms Act-only and standard Chain-of-Thought (CoT) baselines across QA, fact verification, and interactive decision tasks.

evaluated_datasets: APIBench, a comprehensive dataset consisting of HuggingFace, TorchHub and TensorHub APIs, introduced to evaluate API call writing ability and hallucination.
metrics_comparison.quantitative_results: Gorilla surpasses GPT-4 on writing API calls. When combined with a document retriever it demonstrates strong capability to adapt to test-time document changes and substantially mitigates hallucination commonly encountered when prompting LLMs directly. Evaluation shows improved accuracy versus hallucination across settings.
metrics_comparison.baseline_comparison: Consistently outperforms Act-only and standard Chain-of-Thought (CoT) baselines across QA, fact verification, and interactive decision tasks.

evaluated_datasets: Evaluation is conducted in MineDojo, an open-source Minecraft AI framework, with simulation built on MineDojo and Mineflayer JavaScript APIs for motor controls. Text completion uses OpenAI gpt-4-0314 and gpt-3.5-turbo-0301 APIs, with text-embedding-ada-002 for text embedding. All temperatures are set to 0 except the automatic curriculum which uses temperature 0.1 to encourage task diversity. Baselines include LLM-based agent techniques ReAct, Reflexion and AutoGPT re-interpreted for embodiment as no LLM-based agents work out of the box for Minecraft.
metrics_comparison.quantitative_results: VOYAGER demonstrates strong in-context lifelong learning capabilities and constructs an ever-growing skill library of action programs that are reusable, interpretable, and generalizable to novel tasks. Compared to prior LLM-based agents in MineDojo, VOYAGER obtains 3.3x more unique items, unlocks key tech tree milestones up to 15.3x faster, and traverses 2.3x longer distances. VOYAGER can utilize the learned skill library in a new Minecraft world to solve novel tasks from scratch, while other methods struggle to generalize.

evaluated_datasets: HumanEval (Chen et al., 2021a) and MBPP (Austin et al., 2021) for code generation evaluation; collaborative software engineering benchmarks.
metrics_comparison.quantitative_results: MetaGPT generates more coherent solutions than previous chat-based multi-agent systems on collaborative software engineering benchmarks. On code generation benchmarks it achieves a new state-of-the-art Pass@1 of 85.9% on HumanEval and 87.7% on MBPP, outperforming frameworks such as AutoGPT, LangChain and AgentVerse for complex software project creation.
metrics_comparison.baseline_comparison: Consistently outperforms Act-only and standard Chain-of-Thought (CoT) baselines across QA, fact verification, and interactive decision tasks.

metrics_comparison.quantitative_results: Extensive testing over 29 API-based and open-sourced LLMs shows top commercial LLMs present strong ability of acting as agents in complex environments, with a significant performance gap versus many OSS competitors no larger than 70B. Typical failure reasons are poor long-term reasoning, decision-making and instruction following. Improving instruction following and training on high-quality multi-round alignment data can improve agent performance. Code training has ambivalent impacts on different agent tasks, improving some while harming others. Models referenced include gpt-4 (0613), claude-3 (opus), glm-4, codellama-34b-instruct, vicuna-13b-v1.5, llama-2-70b.
metrics_comparison.baseline_comparison: Consistently outperforms Act-only and standard Chain-of-Thought (CoT) baselines across QA, fact verification, and interactive decision tasks.

metrics_comparison.quantitative_results: Customizable and conversable agents enable easy creation of agents with different roles such as code writing, code execution, human feedback wiring, and output validation. Conversation programming streamlines development of intricate applications. AutoGen realizes effective retrieval augmentation and a novel interactive retrieval feature that boosts performance on Q&A tasks. A three-agent system with a grounding agent improves performance on ALFWorld. Multi-agent design boosts performance on coding tasks that need safeguards.
metrics_comparison.baseline_comparison: Consistently outperforms Act-only and standard Chain-of-Thought (CoT) baselines across QA, fact verification, and interactive decision tasks.

evaluated_datasets: SWE-bench comprising 2,294 software engineering problems drawn from real GitHub issues and corresponding pull requests across 12 popular Python repositories.
metrics_comparison.quantitative_results: Evaluations show both state-of-the-art proprietary models and the fine-tuned SWE-Llama can resolve only the simplest issues. The best-performing model, Claude 2, solves a mere 1.96% of the issues.
metrics_comparison.baseline_comparison: Consistently outperforms Act-only and standard Chain-of-Thought (CoT) baselines across QA, fact verification, and interactive decision tasks.

evaluated_datasets: Open-domain QA, multi-hop reasoning, fact verification and long-form generation tasks, including ASQA, QAMPARI, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, MuSiQue and long-form QA datasets for factuality and citation evaluation.
metrics_comparison.quantitative_results: SELF-RAG 7B and 13B significantly outperforms state-of-the-art LLMs and retrieval-augmented models on a diverse set of tasks. Specifically, SELF-RAG outperforms ChatGPT and retrieval-augmented Llama2-chat on open-domain QA, reasoning and fact verification tasks, and shows significant gains in improving factuality and citation accuracy for long-form generation.
